candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Parables (1 Enoch 37-71) (c. 100 BC)

'The second vision which he saw, the vision of wisdom — which Enoch the son of Jared, the son of Mahalalel...' opens the Book of Parables, the most theologically dense section of 1 Enoch. Where the Watchers material is mythological-historical, the Parables are visionary-eschatological, centering on the figure of the Son of Man as cosmic judge. The opening dating in 'the days of Jared' (consistent with 6:6) anchors the Parables historically while the visionary content opens onto the eschaton. The Tewahedo reception of the Parables as canonical Scripture gives the Mäṣḥafä Hēnok its distinctive Christological-eschatological weight.

candidates.draft_body:

'Until the present day such wisdom has never been given by the Lord of Spirits as I have received... that I should declare it to those who dwell on the earth' — Enoch's commissioning to deliver the Parables not as private mysticism but as covenant proclamation. The Tewahedo Synaxarium retains Enoch's prophetic status as one to whom the heavenly wisdom-tradition was entrusted, the textual basis for the liturgical reading of 1 Enoch in select Tewahedo festal contexts.
